slides.1.title: Classic Variety × Region Combinations
slides.1.points.0: Barossa Valley → Old Vine Shiraz (100+ year vines, ultra-concentrated)
slides.1.points.1: Clare Valley + Eden Valley → Riesling (vibrant acidity, lime, slate mineral)
slides.1.points.2: Coonawarra → Cabernet Sauvignon (terra rossa soil, mint and blackcurrant)
slides.1.points.3: Hunter Valley → Sémillon (low alcohol, bottle-aged honey and toast)
slides.1.points.4: Margaret River → Cabernet + Chardonnay (Bordeaux-style reds, Burgundy-style whites)
slides.1.points.5: Tasmania → Pinot Noir + sparkling wines (cool climate, high acidity)
slides.2.title: Variety × Region Visual Matrix
slides.2.points.0: SA Dominance: Barossa (Shiraz), Clare/Eden (Riesling), Coonawarra (Cabernet), McLaren Vale (GSM blend)
slides.2.points.1: VIC Diversity: Yarra (Pinot, Chardonnay), Heathcote (Shiraz), Rutherglen (Muscat), Grampians (Sparkling Shiraz)
slides.2.points.2: NSW Specialities: Hunter (Sémillon), Orange (Chardonnay, Pinot Gris), Mudgee (full-bodied reds)
slides.2.points.3: WA Finesse: Margaret River (Cab, Chardonnay, SBS), Great Southern (Riesling, Shiraz)
slides.2.points.4: TAS Excellence: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, premium sparkling base
slides.3.question: Which region is most celebrated for Sémillon that can age magnificently for 15–20 years?
slides.3.explanation: Hunter Valley (NSW) is the home of Australia's most distinctive Sémillon. Early-harvested at low alcohol (10–11%), it ages without oak for 15–20 years, developing remarkable honey, toast and lanolin complexity. It is one of the world's most unique wine styles.
slides.4.title: Lesson Summary
slides.4.points.0: Classic pairings: Barossa→Shiraz, Clare/Eden→Riesling, Coonawarra→Cabernet, Hunter→Sémillon, Margaret River→Cabernet+Chardonnay, Tasmania→Pinot+Sparkling
slides.4.points.1: SA dominates volume and iconic varieties; WA and TAS lead in boutique quality
slides.4.points.2: Understanding region–variety links is essential for reading Australian wine labels
